heard: two lists of coin flips. The more random one is fake. Don't count heads. Both have about 100. A math professor tells his class, flip a coin 200 times, or fake it. Next day, he spots nearly every faker. His trick, find the longest streak. The same side again and again in a row. Fakers switch sides too often. Six heads in a row feels rigged, so they leave it out. But a six in a row really that normal. Each flip matches the last one half the time. Five matches in a row is one in 32. And in 200 flips, a streak can start in 195 places. So a real list has six in a row, 97 times in 100. No streak of six. Somebody made it up. Flip a coin 20 times. What's your longest streak?
